facts.fact: Science is the systematic search for knowledge of the natural world by observation, experiment and reasoning.
Technology is the application of scientific knowledge to solve practical problems.
Innovation is the successful introduction of a new product, process or service into use.
An invention becomes an innovation only when it is adopted and creates value.
Article 51A(h) makes developing the scientific temper a Fundamental Duty.
Article 51A(h) was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976.
Article 51A(g) is about protecting the natural environment.
The Scientific Policy Resolution (1958, Nehru) aimed to cultivate science and scientific temper.
The Technology Policy Statement (1983) stressed technological self-reliance.
The Science and Technology Policy 2003 (Vajpayee) integrated S&T and raised investment.
STIP 2013 first added 'Innovation' to the policy title with the theme 'STI for the People'.
STIP 2013 set a 2% of GDP GERD goal and a top-five scientific power aim.
Draft STIP 2020 (PSA + DST, decentralised, bottom-up) would be the fifth policy and is not yet notified.
The ANRF was set up by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation Act, 2023.
ANRF subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB, 2008).
ANRF envisages Rs 50,000 crore over 2023-28.
About Rs 36,000 crore of ANRF funding is expected from industry and philanthropy.
The Prime Minister is ex-officio President of ANRF's Governing Board.
The first ANRF Governing Board meeting was held in September 2024.
The Ministry of Science and Technology has three departments: DST, DBT and DSIR.
DST was set up in 1971.
DBT was set up in 1986.
CSIR (1942) works under DSIR and runs about 37 laboratories.
DAE (1954) functions directly under the Prime Minister.
BARC, IGCAR and NPCIL are units of DAE.
ISRO was set up in 1969 and works under the Department of Space.
The Principal Scientific Adviser chairs PM-STIAC.
National Quantum Mission (2023, DST) has an outlay of Rs 6003.65 crore for 2023-24 to 2030-31.
The National Quantum Mission has four thematic hubs (computing, communication, sensing, materials).
The National Supercomputing Mission (2015) builds PARAM supercomputers via C-DAC.
NM-ICPS (2018, about Rs 3,660 crore) set up 25 Technology Innovation Hubs.
The RDI Scheme (2025) has a corpus of about Rs 1 lakh crore for private-sector R&D.
India's GERD is about 0.64% of GDP.
The government funds most of India's R&D; the private share is low.
The Global Innovation Index is published by WIPO.
India ranked 39th (2024) and 38th (2025) in the GII.
One Nation One Subscription became operational on 1 January 2025 via INFLIBNET (UGC).
Vigyan Dhara (2024) merged three DST umbrella schemes.
SDSC-SHAR at Sriharikota is ISRO's primary spaceport.
NARL (an autonomous institute of the Department of Space) is at Gadanki near Tirupati.
IIT Tirupati is at Yerpedu, Tirupati; IISER Tirupati is also at Tirupati.
NIT Andhra Pradesh is at Tadepalligudem.
IIPE is at Visakhapatnam.
AIIMS Mangalagiri is near Guntur.
CCMB, IICT and NGRI are in Hyderabad (Telangana), not Andhra Pradesh.
National Physical Laboratory (NPL) — keeper of Indian Standard Time is located at New Delhi.
National Chemical Laboratory (NCL) is located at Pune.
Central Drug Research Institute (CDRI) is located at Lucknow.
Central Food Technological Research Institute (CFTRI) is located at Mysuru.
Central Leather Research Institute (CLRI) is located at Chennai.
National Institute of Oceanography (NIO) is located at Dona Paula, Goa.
National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) is located at Nagpur.
National Aerospace Laboratories (NAL) — Hansa and Saras aircraft is located at Bengaluru.
Indian Institute of Chemical Technology (IICT) is located at Hyderabad (Telangana).
National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) is located at Hyderabad (Telangana).
Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology (CCMB) is located at Hyderabad (Telangana).
Central Electrochemical Research Institute (CECRI) is located at Karaikudi (Tamil Nadu).
Central Institute of Medicinal and Aromatic Plants (CIMAP) is located at Lucknow.
Central Building Research Institute (CBRI) is located at Roorkee.
Central Scientific Instruments Organisation (CSIO) is located at Chandigarh.
Central Road Research Institute (CRRI) is located at New Delhi.
Indian Institute of Science (1909; vision of Jamsetji Tata) is located at Bengaluru.
Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945; Homi Bhabha) is located at Mumbai.
Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) is located at Trombay, Mumbai.
Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) is located at Kalpakkam (Tamil Nadu).
Physical Research Laboratory (1947; Vikram Sarabhai) is located at Ahmedabad.
Raman Research Institute (1948; C.V. Raman) is located at Bengaluru.
Bose Institute (1917; J.C. Bose) is located at Kolkata.
Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science (1876; Mahendralal Sircar) — where Raman discovered the Raman effect is located at Kolkata.
Saha Institute of Nuclear Physics is located at Kolkata.
National Institute of Virology (ICMR) is located at Pune.
National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR) is located at Hyderabad (Telangana).
Centre for DNA Fingerprinting and Diagnostics (CDFD) is located at Hyderabad (Telangana).
Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services (INCOIS) — tsunami early warning is located at Hyderabad (Telangana).
ICRISAT (dryland crops research) is located at Patancheru, near Hyderabad (Telangana).
Indian Agricultural Research Institute (Pusa Institute, ICAR) is located at New Delhi.
Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences (ARIES) is located at Nainital.
Indian Institute of Astrophysics (runs the Kodaikanal observatory) is located at Bengaluru.
ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research): 1911 (as Indian Research Fund Association) — Ministry of Health (Dept of Health Research).
ICAR (Indian Council of Agricultural Research): 1929 — Ministry of Agriculture (DARE).
DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation): 1958 — Ministry of Defence.
Department of Space: 1972 — directly under the Prime Minister.
Ministry of Earth Sciences: 2006 — runs IMD, INCOIS and NCPOR.
India Meteorological Department (IMD): 1875 — Ministry of Earth Sciences.
Indian Science Congress Association: 1914 — first session at Kolkata.
Indian National Science Academy (INSA): 1935 — New Delhi.
TIFAC (Technology Information, Forecasting and Assessment Council): 1988 — autonomous body under DST.
Vigyan Prasar (science popularisation): 1989 — autonomous body under DST.
First Principal Scientific Adviser (1999): A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
Principal Scientific Adviser 2001–2018: R. Chidambaram.
Principal Scientific Adviser appointed in April 2022: Ajay Kumar Sood (after K. VijayRaghavan, 2018–2022).
National Science Day: 28 February — discovery of the Raman effect (1928).
National Technology Day: 11 May — Pokhran-II nuclear tests (1998).
National Mathematics Day: 22 December — Srinivasa Ramanujan's birthday.
Rashtriya Vigyan Puraskar (from 2023): new national science awards — Vigyan Ratna, Vigyan Shri, Vigyan Yuva-Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar and Vigyan Team.
Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize: top science prize for scientists under 45 (from 1958); now part of the Vigyan Yuva award.
INSPIRE (Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research): 2008, DST — draws school and college students into science (absorbed KVPY in 2022).
Atal Innovation Mission: 2016, NITI Aayog — Atal Tinkering Labs in schools and Atal Incubation Centres.
Vigyan Jyoti: DST scheme (2019) encouraging girls in Classes 9–12 to take up STEM.
KIRAN (now WISE-KIRAN): DST scheme (2014) supporting women scientists.
NIDHI: DST's 2016 programme to nurture ideas and start-ups through incubators.
Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF): 2018 — PhD fellowships at IITs, IISc and other top institutions.
VAIBHAV fellowship: 2023 — links Indian-origin scientists abroad with Indian institutions.
India Semiconductor Mission: 2021 — ₹76,000 crore for chip fabs and display units.
IndiaAI Mission: March 2024 — about ₹10,372 crore for AI compute, datasets and models.
Deep Ocean Mission: 2021, Ministry of Earth Sciences — Samudrayaan crewed submersible Matsya-6000 (6,000 m).
National Geospatial Policy: 2022 — opened up mapping data for Indian firms.
RDI Scheme approval: approved by the Union Cabinet in July 2025; its fund is run through the ANRF.
National IPR Policy: May 2016 — slogan "Creative India; Innovative India"; nodal department DPIIT.
Term of a patent in India: 20 years from the date of filing.
Patents Act: 1970 (in force from 1972); amended in 2005 to bring in product patents.
Geographical Indications of Goods Act: 1999 (in force from 2003); a GI is registered for 10 years and can be renewed.
India's first GI tag: Darjeeling tea (2004).
TRIPS Agreement: WTO agreement on intellectual property (1995).
Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Act: 2001 — protects plant breeders and farmers.
Copyright Act: 1957.
Trade Marks Act: 1999.
Tirupati laddu — temple prasadam of Tirumala (GI 2009).
Araku Valley Arabica coffee — tribal coffee of the Eastern Ghats, Alluri Sitharama Raju district (GI 2019).
Banganapalle mango — mango variety of Kurnool / Nandyal region (GI 2017).
Kondapalli toys — light-wood toys of Kondapalli, NTR district.
Etikoppaka toys — lacquer-coated wooden toys of Anakapalli district.
Srikalahasti Kalamkari — hand-painted (pen) Kalamkari textiles of Srikalahasti.
Mangalagiri sarees and fabrics — handloom cotton of Mangalagiri, Guntur district.
Uppada Jamdani sarees — silk Jamdani weaving of Uppada, Kakinada district.
Sriharikota (SDSC-SHAR) — Tirupati district (earlier SPSR Nellore district).
Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL, DRDO) — Visakhapatnam.
Central Tobacco Research Institute (ICAR) — Rajahmundry.
Indian Institute of Oil Palm Research (ICAR) — Pedavegi, Eluru district.
IIITDM (Indian Institute of Information Technology, Design and Manufacturing) — Kurnool.
IIIT Sri City — Sri City, Tirupati district.
IIM Visakhapatnam — Visakhapatnam.
Central University of Andhra Pradesh — Anantapur.
Central Tribal University of Andhra Pradesh — Vizianagaram.
Amaravati Quantum Valley — planned around an IBM Quantum System Two (156-qubit Heron processor), with TCS and L&T.
Andhra University (1926) — Visakhapatnam.
Sri Venkateswara University (1954) — Tirupati.
